'''Ajith Kumar''' (1952–March 1, 2025)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Butler |first=Rhett Ayers |date=2025-03-02 |title=Indian wildlife biologist Ajith Kumar has died |url=https://news.mongabay.com/short-article/indian-wildlife-biologist-ajith-kumar-dies-at-72/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Mongabay Environmental News |language=en-US}}</ref> was an Indian [[wildlife biologist]] and [[Conservation biology|conservationist]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Devarajan |first=Kadambari |date=2025-03-22 |title=An unparalleled conservationist |url=https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/open-page/an-unparalleled-conservationist/article69334133.ece |access-date=2025-03-27 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> well known for his contributions to the ecology and conservation of [[Primate|primates]] such as the [[Endangered species|endangered]] [[lion-tailed macaque]], and [[Small mammal|small mammals]], with a career spanning over four decades of research,<ref>{{Cite web |last=India |first=C. W. S. |date=2025-03-02 |title=A Tribute to Dr. Ajith Kumar: Extraordinary Wildlife Biologist, Beloved Mentor and Friend - Centre for Wildlife Studies |url=https://cwsindia.org/tribute-dr-ajith-kumar/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Talk by Dr. Ajit Kumar, India's Leading Primatologist, CWS, Bangalore, Nov 08, 2019 |url=https://www.conservationindia.org/events/talk-by-dr-ajit-kumar-indias-leading-primatologist-cws-bangalore-nov-08-2019 |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Conservation India |language=en-US}}</ref> teaching<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty {{!}} Masters in Wildlife Biology & Conservation |url=https://www.ncbs.res.in/mscprogram/faculty |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=www.ncbs.res.in}}</ref> and conservation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ministry of Environment & Forests & Climate Change, Government of India |date=2 October 2014 |title=List of experts for preparation of Wildlife Management Plan |url=https://moef.gov.in/uploads/2018/03/F.No_.6-1332014-Wl(Pt.)List%20of%20experts%20%20for%20WLMP34.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241005071517/https://moef.gov.in/uploads/2018/03/F.No_.6-1332014-Wl(Pt.)List%20of%20experts%20%20for%20WLMP34.pdf |archive-date=2024-10-05 |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=moef.gov.in |url-status=live }}</ref> His work contributed significantly to the understanding of rainforest ecology, [[habitat fragmentation]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Sivaganesan |first1=N |url=https://www.sacon.in/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/1998-PR69.pdf |title=Status of wildlife corridors and their use by mammals with special reference to selected endangered mammals in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve |last2=Kumar |first2=Ajith |date=March 1997 |publisher=Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology & Natural History }}</ref> and species conservation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-01 |title=Talk on Lion-Tailed Macaque held at Mysuru Zoo |url=https://starofmysore.com/talk-on-lion-tailed-macaque-held-at-mysuru-zoo/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Star of Mysore |language=en-US}}</ref> Along with [[K. Ullas Karanth|Ullas Karanth]] and other collaborators, he was instrumental in establishing a Masters course in wildlife biology and conservation<ref>{{Cite web |title=Against the tide: NCBS's wildlife students {{!}} NCBS news |url=https://news.ncbs.res.in/archivednews/story/against-tide-ncbss-wildlife-students |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=news.ncbs.res.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Subramanyan |first=Shamala Kittane |date=2013-03-03 |title=Can you get a degree in wildlife in India? |url=https://citizenmatters.in/4977-know-more-about-the-national-centre-for-biological-sciences/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Citizen Matters |language=en-US}}</ref> at the [[National Centre for Biological Sciences]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Collection: Ajith Kumar Papers {{!}} Archives at NCBS |url=https://catalogue.archives.ncbs.res.in/repositories/2/resources/17 |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=catalogue.archives.ncbs.res.in}}</ref> serving as the founding course director from its inception in 2004 till 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Dr. Ajith Kumar (1953–2025) |url=https://www.wti.org.in/news/in-memoriam-dr-ajith-kumar-1955-2025/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Wildlife Trust of India |language=en-US}}</ref> His early field notes and works have been archived<ref name=":0" /> in the NCBS Archives initiative, a public collecting centre for the history of science in contemporary India.<ref name=":0" /> He served as a member of the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]] Primate Specialist Group which aims to "promote research on the ecology and conservation of hundreds of primate species".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Primates-SG - Home |url=http://www.primate-sg.org/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=www.primate-sg.org |language=en}}</ref>
